name: Austin Bergstrom International Airport
before:
Austin's airport, about 5 miles south east of downtown, third busiest in Texas after Dallas Fort Worth and Houston Intercontinental, and 27th busiest in the United States. As of 2023 it ran more than 550 arrivals and departures on a typical weekday to 97 destinations across North America and Europe.

Everything goes through one building. The Barbara Jordan Terminal has 34 gates, of which only six can handle international flights, so international capacity is much tighter than the overall size suggests. Lounges are run by American, Delta and United.

It has a genuinely Austin touch: a live music stage in the terminal where local bands perform, in keeping with the city's claim to be the live music capital of the world. Note that all but two of the food outlets are past security.

The airport sits on the former Bergstrom Air Force Base, decommissioned in the early 1990s, and replaced Robert Mueller Municipal Airport as Austin's main airport in 1999.
after:
Austin's airport, about 8 miles south east of downtown. With about 21.7 million passengers in 2025, it is the third busiest airport in Texas, after Dallas/Fort Worth and George Bush Intercontinental in Houston, and one of the 30 busiest in the United States. Nonstop flights reach destinations across North America and Europe.

The airport says all its airlines have used the main Barbara Jordan Terminal since 1 April 2026, when the South Terminal closed. Almost all the places to eat are past security. Local musicians play at venues in the terminal on weekdays, in keeping with Austin's claim to be the Live Music Capital of the World.

The airport sits on the former Bergstrom Air Force Base, which was decommissioned in the early 1990s. It replaced Robert Mueller Municipal Airport as Austin's main airport in 1999.

claims.claim: about 8 miles south east of downtown
claims.inAfter: Austin's airport, about 8 miles south east of downtown.
claims.note: Was 'about 5 miles', which fails the coordinates check: the straight line from the GeoNames centre is 6.8 miles (11.0 km), a ratio of 0.73. The written sources differ: Wikipedia 5 miles, the FAA master record 5 nautical miles (about 5.8 miles) from its business-district point, the City's own history page eight miles from the Capitol. The text follows the operator, whose figure passes the coordinates check as a road-style distance (ratio 1.18). South east is in every source.

claims.note: New to the text, replacing the 2023 flight and destination counts as the measure of how busy it is. TOTAL passengers, both terminals, arriving plus departing: 21,666,852 in 2025, down 0.44 per cent on 21,762,904 in 2024 (operator's December 2025 report; its enplaned and deplaned totals, 10,857,912 and 10,808,940, add up to it). The operator's FAQ says 2023 was the record year, with over 22 million, so 2025 is not called a record. The FAA's preliminary CY2025 table counts 10,651,727 enplanements (boardings only, about half of total passengers), in line with the operator's enplaned total.

claims.claim: the airport says all its airlines have used the Barbara Jordan Terminal since 1 April 2026, when the South Terminal closed
claims.inAfter: The airport says all its airlines have used the main Barbara Jordan Terminal since 1 April 2026, when the South Terminal closed.
claims.note: Replaces 'Everything goes through one building', which rested on Wikipedia calling the Barbara Jordan Terminal the 'main' terminal. The separate South Terminal, used by Allegiant and Frontier, carried 771,354 passengers in 2025 and closed after 31 March 2026; it is being removed for new taxiways. An attributed statement, as for Timisoara: the only source is the airport's own page, because Allegiant's site refused the browser (403), Frontier's airport page has no Austin entry and no news page could be found without a search engine. Worth Andy's eye.
